To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have demonstrated a new approach for the estimation of the power level of acoustic sources in noisy environments using the spectral estimation method for additive noise and a noise reference.

a new technique has been developed for the power level estimation of multiple sources in a noisy environment, using a noise reference, that has the advantage of providing accurate results, with low computational requirements, and that has been successfully applied to both simulated and experimental data.

we propose and test a new spectral estimation method for noisy acoustic data using a noise-reference that allows us to estimate the power levels of acoustic sources in a noisy environment with good accuracy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method for estimating the acoustic power levels of sources in a noise environment.
the development of a new method of spectral estimation for the estimation of acoustic sources power levels in a noisy environment using a noise reference signal.
the development of a technique that can be used in practical applications for the estimation of the absolute levels of multiple acoustic sources in the presence of additive noise.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed approach is a promising alternative for the accurate power level estimation of multiple acoustic sources.
, in this work, a new method has been presented for the power level estimation of a source radiating in a background noise.

the method proposed is able to provide the correct source levels with a very high accuracy, in a very short time and with a very good spatial resolution, in the presence of a high level of background noise.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed method is a good alternative to other methods, such as the conventional beamforming and deconvolution methods, for the extraction of acoustic source levels from the measured sound fields.
a new spectral estimation method for noisy acoustic data using a noise source as a reference has been proposed, tested and validated for both computer and experimental simulations.
we have developed a new technique that can estimate the source level of an acoustic source with good accuracy and that is robust in the presence of background noise.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the spectral estimation method with noise reference is able to estimate the power levels of acoustic sources in noisy environments with a high level of accuracy.
, in the presence of a noise reference, the proposed spectral estimation method with noise reference is able to provide a good estimate of the source levels, with a very low background noise level.
the use of an appropriate noise reference can be very effective in improving the accuracy of the source levels estimated using beamforming techniques.
